- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 1–4% per day of negative sentiment.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 60–70% of 30d range), especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture reversion.
- For 30d horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (days 1–7); cap first 5 days’ forecast at 1% below the 18-day moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5 or 0.5–1.0), model tends to err on the high side; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
